tryFirstPrompt: You have a plain JavaScript variable inside a React component, and a button that increments it and logs the new value. The log shows the number going up, but the screen never changes. Why do you think the screen is stuck?
explanationShort: useState gives a component a value that survives re-renders plus a setter that tells React the value changed. A plain variable does neither: it is recreated on every render, and changing it never tells React to draw again.
explanationLong: Calling useState(0) returns [value, setValue]. React stores the value outside the function, keyed by where the hook was called, so it persists across renders; a plain `let count = 0` is re-initialised every time the function body runs. The second half matters just as much: calling setValue marks the component dirty and schedules a re-render, which is the step a plain assignment skips entirely. That is why the log in the question goes up while the screen does not — the number really is changing, but nothing has asked React to redraw. setValue also does not mutate the current value: within the same render `value` keeps the value it had when that render started, which is why you pass a function like setCount(c => c + 1) when the next value depends on the previous one.

corrections.wrong: The screen doesn't update because the variable isn't changing.
corrections.why: It is changing — the log proves it. What's missing is the signal to React that it should re-render; a plain assignment updates the value silently.

corrections.wrong: After calling setCount, count holds the new value on the next line.
corrections.why: It doesn't. `count` is fixed for the whole of the current render, and the new value only appears in the next one. Reading it straight after the setter gives you the old number.

corrections.wrong: useState is basically a component-scoped global variable.
corrections.why: It's per component instance, not per component. Two copies of the same component on screen each get their own independent state.
